key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on the connections of analogue neural networks makes them far more efficient for smooth, continuous control tasks than standard weight-only physical networks.
engineering_relevance: This points to a low-power hardware path for continuous control and energy systems, with a projected CMOS implementation around 30 microwatts.
method: Use connection-level trainable nonlinearities instead of scalar weights.
Implement the nonlinear connections as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Test transfer to hardware and simulate a memristive version to confirm device-agnostic behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better parameter efficiency on smooth targets such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, with quantified transfer across about 35,000 connections.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and does not extend to classification-like decision boundaries, so it may not help all AI workloads.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
